title: Ecology — Concepts and Ecosystems
topicTitle: Ecosystem ecology: concept of ecology, biotic and abiotic factors, species interactions; concept of ecosystem, structural and functional aspects of pond and forest ecosystem
confusion: ❌ Ecology is the same as environmental science. ✅ Ecology studies organism-environment interactions; environmental science is broader, including policy and chemistry.
❌ Biotic factors are non-living. ✅ Biotic = living (plants, animals, microbes); Abiotic = non-living (light, temperature, water).
❌ Abiotic factors don't affect species distribution. ✅ Abiotic factors (temperature, pH, salinity) are primary determinants of where organisms live.
❌ Competition always benefits both species. ✅ Competition harms both (−/−); mutualism benefits both (+/+); predation benefits one, harms other (+/−).
❌ A food chain shows all feeding relationships. ✅ Food chain is linear; food web shows interconnected, complex feeding relationships.
❌ 90% of energy transfers to the next trophic level. ✅ Only ~10% transfers; ~90% lost as heat at each level (10% rule).
❌ Biomagnification decreases toxin concentration up the food chain. ✅ Biomagnification increases toxin concentration at higher trophic levels.
❌ An ecosystem includes only living organisms. ✅ Ecosystem = biotic community + abiotic environment interacting as a system.
❌ Pond and forest ecosystems have the same structure. ✅ Pond: aquatic, open water column, phytoplankton-dominated; Forest: terrestrial, stratified canopy, detritus-dominated.
❌ Producers are at the top of the food chain. ✅ Producers (autotrophs) are always at the base (first trophic level).
❌ Energy flows in cycles in an ecosystem. ✅ Energy flows unidirectionally (sun→producers→consumers→heat); nutrients cycle.
❌ Decomposers are not part of the food chain. ✅ Decomposers (bacteria, fungi) recycle nutrients from all trophic levels.
❌ A biome and an ecosystem are the same thing. ✅ Biome = large-scale community (e.g., tropical rainforest); Ecosystem = specific community + environment in an area.
❌ Ecological succession always leads to a forest. ✅ Climax community depends on climate; tundra succession stops at grassland/shrubland.
❌ Primary succession starts with soil already present. ✅ Primary succession starts on bare rock/substrate with no soil; secondary starts with existing soil.
❌ In a pond ecosystem, plants are only at the bottom. ✅ Pond has floating plants (phytoplankton), emergent (reeds), submerged (hydrilla), and littoral zone plants.
❌ Forest ecosystems have uniform temperature year-round. ✅ Forests have vertical stratification (canopy, understory, forest floor) with different microclimates.
❌ Species interactions only involve animals. ✅ Interactions include plants-pollinators, plants-herbivores, microbes-decomposers, etc.
❌ The biosphere is the same as the atmosphere. ✅ Biosphere = all living zones (atmosphere + hydrosphere + lithosphere where life exists).
❌ Ecological pyramids can be inverted for energy. ✅ Energy pyramid is never inverted; biomass/number pyramids can be (e.g., one tree → many insects).
